--- title: "Simulation Based Estimation of Sampling Bias" jupyter: python3 fig-dpi: 300 bibliography: references.bib --- ```{=html} ``` # Data and models **Field.** GLORYS12V1 reanalysis on its native $1/12^\circ$ grid. OHC is the $0$–$2000$ m depth integral of potential temperature against constant $c_p\rho$ (`code/ohc.py`), evaluated daily over 2010–2019. Cells enter the analysis only where $\mathrm{deptho} > 2000$ m *and* the integral is defined at every level, which is $92.4\%$ of Box B by area ($26{,}785$ cells) and $99.8\%$ of Box A ($34{,}863$ cells) — Box B loses its shelf edge, Box A is essentially all deep ocean. **Mean field.** OHC is split as $\mathrm{OHC} = \hat m + \tilde Z$ into a smooth climatological mean field $\hat m$, fitted once across $1995$–$2019$, and the residual $\tilde Z_k$ the designs actually sample — the field the sampling bias is defined over. $\hat m$ is a per-cell OLS on a quadratic trend plus annual and semiannual harmonics, fit against the GLORYS *monthly* record with each basis function averaged over its month to match the monthly-mean response, then evaluated pointwise per day. @sec-meanfield gives the estimator and summarizes what it leaves. **Advection.** OceanParcels, park depth $1000$ m, advected by GLORYS daily $(u,v)$ over $15$–$50^\circ$ N, $70$–$30^\circ$ W. Floats advect continuously at park depth and record a position every $10$ days; there is no ascent, descent or surface drift, so a cycle is a position sample, not a simulated dive. Floats are deleted on leaving the velocity domain and retired at a lifespan drawn from the real Argo record for this region ($153$ deployments, median $1339$ d). **Estimation.** $\hat Z$ is the unweighted mean of $\tilde Z_k$ at the profile positions, and $\bar Z_k$ is the exact $\mathbb{P}$-weighted domain mean of the same field. # The analysis domain Two analysis boxes sit inside the downloaded GLORYS region, both spanning $60^\circ$–$40^\circ$ W: **Box B** ($35$–$45^\circ$ N) straddles the North Atlantic Current and the Gulf Stream extension, and **Box A** ($22$–$34^\circ$ N) sits in the quiescent subtropical gyre. Temperature is downloaded over a common buffer, from which the OHC truth and the fitted mean field are built; velocity is downloaded over a larger region, because floats seeded near a box advect well outside it and return, and a float that leaves the velocity domain is lost from the experiment rather than merely lost from the box. ::: {#cell-fig-domain .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Analysis boxes inside the two downloaded GLORYS regions. Dashed: the velocity region driving advection, and the thetao region from which OHC truth and the mean field are built. Filled: the two analysis boxes.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-domain-output-1.png){#fig-domain width=821 height=716} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-bathy .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![GLORYS ocean depth over the advection domain. Left: deptho in km, capped at 6 km for display so the shelf break is resolved rather than compressed against the abyssal plain. Right: the ocean cells shallower than the 2000 m analysis cut, which are excluded from the OHC integral and from the measure P. Both analysis boxes are outlined. Land is grey in both panels.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-bathy-output-1.png){#fig-bathy width=1402 height=605} ::: ::: @fig-bathy is why the analysis mask is not the whole box. OHC is integrated to $2000$ m, so a cell enters the estimand only where the water column reaches that depth; $88.7\%$ of the ocean cells in the advection domain do. The cut is not evenly distributed. **Box B loses $7.2\%$ of its area to it**, and that loss is concentrated in one corner: $99\%$ of its excluded cells lie north of $42^\circ$ N and $81\%$ west of $50^\circ$ W, on the Grand Banks and the Newfoundland shelf and rise. **Box A loses $0.08\%$** — $29$ cells, all isolated ridge and seamount tops in its eastern half. Median depth is $4.85$ km in Box B and $4.94$ km in Box A. The mask actually used is slightly stricter than the depth cut alone: it also requires the depth integral to be defined at every level, which drops a further $0.5\%$ of Box B and $0.15\%$ of Box A. Retained area is $92.35\%$ and $99.77\%$ against $92.83\%$ and $99.92\%$ from depth alone. ::: {#cell-fig-days .cell execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Residual field Z on single unaveraged days, in GJ per m2. Each day is the one whose P-weighted spatial standard deviation is nearest the 5th, 50th and 95th percentile of that box's 3,650 daily values, so the columns span typical low, median and high spatial variability. Rows carry their own colour scale, since the boxes differ several-fold in amplitude. Panel titles give the day and its spatial sd.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-days-output-1.png){#fig-days width=1323 height=765} ::: ::: @fig-days is the field the designs actually sample, shown unaveraged: each panel is one real day, selected by where its spatial dispersion $\mathrm{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(\tilde Z_k(\cdot,d))$ falls in the distribution of all $3{,}650$ days. The same construction applied to the flow that moves the floats gives @fig-vel-u and @fig-vel-v: the two park-depth velocity components, each on the day whose own $\mathbb{P}$-weighted spatial standard deviation sits at the 5th, 50th and 95th percentile of that component's $3{,}650$ daily values. The velocity archive is on the identical native grid and is defined at every cell of the analysis mask, so these are the same measure $\mathbb{P}$ and the same cells as @fig-days — no regridding and no second mask. Values are interpolated to the $1000$ m park depth between the two archived levels ($902$ and $1062$ m), which is what Parcels does to the same files when it advects the floats. ::: {#cell-fig-vel-u .cell execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Eastward velocity at 1000 m in cm/s.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-vel-u-output-1.png){#fig-vel-u width=1308 height=766} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-vel-v .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Northward velocity at 1000 m in cm/s.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-vel-v-output-1.png){#fig-vel-v width=1308 height=762} ::: ::: **The flow is roughly twice as disperse in Box B, and that holds on every day, not just energetic ones.** Median daily $\mathrm{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}$ is $12.1$ cm/s eastward and $11.5$ northward in Box B against $5.5$ and $5.4$ in Box A, and the decade-wide range of that daily value is narrow in both — $9.7$–$14.8$ and $9.0$–$14.7$ in Box B, $4.5$–$7.0$ and $4.4$–$6.7$ in Box A. The 5th and 95th percentile columns are therefore much closer to each other than the two rows are, so the box, not the day, is what sets the scale. **Box B's structure is substantially standing, Box A's is substantially transient.** The $\mathbb{P}$-weighted spatial sd of the decade-mean velocity field is $4.11$ cm/s eastward and $2.37$ northward in Box B against $0.94$ and $0.61$ in Box A — a $4.4\times$ and $3.9\times$ gap, about twice the gap in the daily dispersion. As a fraction of each box's mean daily spatial sd, the persistent part is $0.34$ and $0.21$ in Box B against $0.17$ and $0.11$ in Box A. **Neither box has appreciable net transport.** The domain-mean velocity is within $\pm 1$ cm/s of zero on every one of the $3{,}650$ days in both components and both boxes (largest $0.996$ cm/s), so the contrast between the boxes is in spatial structure, not in bulk flow through the domain. Together with @fig-days this is the setup the two boxes were selected to contrast: they differ $3.3\times$ in field amplitude and $2.2\times$ in the daily spatial dispersion of the flow that samples it, with the standing component of that flow differing by about $4\times$. # Mean field {#sec-meanfield} The sampling-bias question concerns the *residual* OHC field, not the total. The smooth climatological part of OHC is large and slowly varying, and any array recovers it almost exactly, so the bias $B$ lives entirely in what remains once it is removed. We therefore decompose $$\mathrm{OHC}(c,t) \;=\; \hat m(c,t) \;+\; \tilde Z(c,t),$$ with $\hat m$ a mean field fitted once across all years — a climatology, deliberately not a per-year fit — and $\tilde Z_k$ the year-$k$ residual the designs sample. Because $\hat m$ is estimated, so is $\tilde Z$; this section states the estimator and summarizes what it leaves. **Regression.** For each analysis cell $c$, OHC is modelled as $\mathrm{OHC}(c,t) = \phi(t)^\top \beta_c + \varepsilon(c,t)$ on the trend-plus-harmonics basis $\phi(t) = \bigl(1,\,t,\,t^2,\,\sin 2\pi t,\,\cos 2\pi t,\,\sin 4\pi t,\,\cos 4\pi t\bigr)^\top$ ($t$ in years): a quadratic secular trend and the annual and semiannual cycles. The coefficients are fit by ordinary least squares to the $1995$–$2019$ GLORYS *monthly* record. **Fit and prediction use different bases, on purpose.** A GLORYS monthly file holds the month *mean* OHC over $I_m = [t_0^m, t_1^m)$ but is time-stamped at its start $t_0^m$. Regressing that mean on the instantaneous basis $\phi(t_0^m)$ would misdate the harmonics by $\sim\!15$ d and attenuate their amplitude, since the mean of a sinusoid over a month is not its value at a point. We instead regress on the **window-averaged basis** $\bar\phi(I_m) = |I_m|^{-1}\!\int_{I_m}\phi(t)\,dt$, so both sides of the regression are monthly averages; each column is exact in closed form (constant $\mapsto 1$; linear $\mapsto$ the window midpoint; quadratic $\mapsto (t_1^3 - t_0^3)/3|I_m|$; each harmonic $\mapsto$ its exact windowed integral). The window is common to every cell, so there is a single design matrix $\bar X = \bigl[\bar\phi(I_m)^\top\bigr]_m$ and the per-cell fit is one pseudo-inverse, $\hat\beta_c = \bar X^{+} Y_c$. **Prediction is then pointwise:** the fitted field is evaluated at each instant on the daily grid, $\hat m(c,t) = \phi(t)^\top \hat\beta_c$, and subtracted from daily OHC to give $\tilde Z_k = \mathrm{OHC}_k - \hat m$ on the same mask. The window average enters only the fit, to keep regressor and response on the same footing; the prediction is the smooth curve itself. ::: {#cell-fig-meanfield .cell execution_count=7} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Fitted mean field (quadratic trend plus annual and semiannual harmonics) at mid-month, 2015, in GJ per m2.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-meanfield-output-1.png){#fig-meanfield width=1484 height=762} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-decomp3 .cell execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![The decomposition on one day per box, in GJ per m2.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-decomp3-output-1.png){#fig-decomp3 width=1024 height=1116} ::: ::: In @fig-decomp3 the identity $\mathrm{OHC} = \hat m + \tilde Z$ holds exactly on the analysis mask: the top row is reconstructed from the other two rather than re-integrated from temperature, and reproduces the GLORYS field bitwise. OHC runs $60$–$90$ GJ/m$^2$ and is almost entirely captured by the smooth mean field; $\tilde Z$ is a few GJ/m$^2$ of mesoscale structure. On the Box B day shown, domain-mean OHC is $67.9$ GJ/m$^2$ against a mean field of $66.5$ and a residual of $+1.45$. The mean field varies on two time scales, neither daily: the harmonics move the Box B domain mean by $3.80$ GJ/m$^2$ within a year ($1.50$ in Box A), the trend by $2.59$ across 2010–2019 ($0.96$), and consecutive days by $0.03$. Everything mesoscale and day-to-day is therefore left in $\tilde Z$ — the field whose domain mean the sampling must recover. **Stationarity caveat.** A single global trend-plus-harmonics form is a preliminary, stationary-in-form choice; OHC is strongly non-stationary across these current regions, so a covariance-aware mean is a likely refinement. It does not threaten $B$: a spatially uniform misfit in $\tilde Z_k$ differences out of $B$ identically, and the per-year residual offsets it leaves are carried explicitly in @tbl-truth rather than assumed zero. # Estimand, truth, and estimator Let $\mathbb{P}$ be the normalized area $\times$ time probability measure on the Box B analysis domain: the base measure is surface measure restricted to the wet native GLORYS cells ($\mathrm{deptho} > 2000$ m, intersected with the data support), $A_j = e1t_j\,e2t_j$, tensored with counting measure on the $365$ days of the year and normalized. The target is the residual field's domain mean, $$\bar Z_k \;=\; \int_{\mathcal{X}} \tilde Z_k \, d\mathbb{P},$$ for each analysis year $k$, where $\tilde Z_k$ is the year-$k$ OHC 0–2000 m field with the fitted mean field removed. A design is a finite point set $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^{n} \subset \mathcal{X}$ — the year-$k$ in-box profiles of one deployment realization $d$; its estimator and bias are $$\hat Z^{(d)}_k \;=\; \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \tilde Z_k\!\left(x_i^{(d)}\right), \qquad B^{(d)}_k \;=\; \hat Z^{(d)}_k - \bar Z_k .$$ $\tilde Z_k$ is a simple function on the native $1/12^\circ \times$ daily grid, so evaluating it at $x_i$ is the cell-day lookup of the *containing* cell, not an interpolation — no quadrature remainder enters. ::: {#tbl-truth .cell execution_count=9} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ```{=html}

The dispersion $\mathrm{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(\tilde Z_k)$ — $6.3$–$7.6$ GJ/m$^2$ in Box B against $1.7$–$2.4$ in Box A, and rising through the decade in Box B — is the $\sigma_k$ that any cross-box comparison of $B$ must be standardized by. # Deployment One continuous advection per realization generates the sampling. For realization $d$, $N$ floats are seeded uniformly over normalized spacetime across the velocity record — area-uniform over the deep ($\mathrm{deptho} \ge 1000$ m) part of a single region spanning both boxes plus an $8^\circ$ margin, uniform in release time — and advected once at park depth. A profile is scored against whichever box contains it, so one deployment feeds both boxes. The lead from the deployment start to the first scored year (several years, against an empirical lifespan median of $1339$ d) brings the drifting array to renewal equilibrium, so the in-box standing stock is flat across the analysis years by construction, with no calibrated release schedule. Each realization therefore yields $B^{(d)}_k$ for every analysis year at once, flow and field the same calendar year — there is no velocity-year / field-year pairing, only the realized diagonal. **Reference.** For a design's per-(box, year) sample size $n$, an $n$-matched iid draw from $\mathbb{P}$ (cell $\propto A_j$, day-of-year uniform) is a genuine sample from $\mathbb{P}$ with $\mathbb{E}[B] = 0$ — at once the null reference and an end-to-end check of the gather, the day-of-year indexing, and the $\bar Z_k$ subtraction. # The sampling weight field The bias is a projection: $B^{(d)}_k = \langle \tilde Z_k,\, w^{(d)} - p\rangle$, the inner product of the residual field with the excess of the empirical sampling weight $w^{(d)}$ over the uniform weight $p_{c,d} = A_c / (\sum_c A_c \cdot 365)$. Averaging the empirical weight over realizations estimates $\mathbb{E}[w]$ — the normalized occupancy measure of the advective array — so $\mathbb{E}[B_k] = \langle \tilde Z_k,\, \mathbb{E}[w] - p\rangle$. This section shows $\mathbb{E}[w]$ on the native $1/12^\circ \times$ daily grid for the scored years $2015$–$2019$. $\mathbb{E}[w]$ lives on spacetime, so it is shown through its spatial and temporal marginals. These are projections: the bias is the *joint* inner product, and does **not** split additively into a space and a time part — a space–time interaction remains, and only the temporal marginal carries an exact bias component $\sum_d (\mathbb{E}[w^t_d] - \tfrac1{365})\,\bar Z_k(d)$. ## Spatial marginal ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Box B ::: {#cell-fig-wspace .cell execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Box B. The spread around 1 measures how preferential the sampling is.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-whist-output-1.png){#fig-whist width=1417 height=318} ::: ::: ### Box A ::: {#cell-fig-wspace-a .cell execution_count=12} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Box A, same construction. The subtropical gyre spreads floats more evenly, so the weight sits closer to uniform than Box B's.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-wspace-a-output-1.png){#fig-wspace-a width=1156 height=353} ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-whist-a .cell execution_count=13} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Box A, same construction as the Box B weight histogram.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-whist-a-output-1.png){#fig-whist-a width=1417 height=318} ::: ::: ::: On the analysis mask the advective array departs from uniform but not wildly: the per-cell weight has standard deviation $\approx 0.46$ (Box B) and $0.37$ (Box A) around a mean of $1$, most cells within a factor of two and the 99th percentile near $2\times$. Box B is the more preferential of the two, and its over-sampled cells cluster where the North Atlantic Current concentrates floats. The strongest concentration happens in shallow, sub-$2000$ m cells *outside* the mask, where it cannot enter $B$; what remains on-mask is the moderate structure shown here, consistent with the small measured bias. ## Temporal marginal ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Box B ::: {#cell-fig-wtime .cell execution_count=14} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Box B. Seasonal marginal of the sampling weight: E[w] per day-of-year against uniform, one line per year. Near 1 throughout means no seasonal sampling bias.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-wtime-output-1.png){#fig-wtime width=869 height=363} ::: ::: ### Box A ::: {#cell-fig-wtime-a .cell execution_count=15} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Box A, same construction.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-wtime-a-output-1.png){#fig-wtime-a width=859 height=363} ::: ::: ::: The day-of-year weight stays within a few percent of uniform all year in both boxes. This is **by construction, and deliberately so**: floats profile on a fixed $10$-day cadence independent of season, release phases are uniform, and the multi-year lead holds the within-year standing stock flat, so no part of the design profiles preferentially in any season. We are therefore not modelling the mechanisms that drive *temporal* sampling bias in real observing systems — seasonal deployment surges, under-ice winter gaps, seasonally varying mortality or cycle timing — an assumption that is defensible for ice-free, mid-latitude Box B, where real Argo also cycles year-round, but is an assumption, not a result. Removing the seasonal marginal by design is the point: it isolates the two mechanisms that are genuinely dynamical — spatial preference and the space–time interaction — so that any bias the array shows is attributable to *where* it samples and to how that *where* co-varies with the field through the year, not to *when*. The residual few-percent wiggle is weak seasonal in/out-advection at the $1000$ m park depth, not a sampling choice. ## Bias as a covariance Write the sampling density ratio as the Radon–Nikodym derivative $r = \mathrm{d}w/\mathrm{d}p$ ($r_{c,d} = w_{c,d}/p_{c,d}$, so $\mathbb{E}_p[r] = 1$). The bias is then exactly a covariance under the uniform measure, $$B_k \;=\; \langle \tilde Z_k,\, w - p\rangle \;=\; \operatorname{Cov}_p\!\big(r,\, \tilde Z_k\big) \;=\; \rho_k \,\operatorname{sd}_p(r)\,\sigma_k,$$ with $\sigma_k = \operatorname{sd}_p(\tilde Z_k)$ (@tbl-truth) and $\rho_k$ the weight–field correlation. Cauchy–Schwarz gives the distribution-free cap $|B_k| \le \operatorname{sd}_p(r)\,\sigma_k$. **Zero bias does not require uniform sampling** — it requires only $\rho_k = 0$, the excess weight orthogonal to the field; a strongly non-uniform array can be unbiased for this functional. Two caveats make this operational. A finite design is discrete, so the pointwise $r$ is unbounded and the exact joint $\operatorname{sd}_p(r)$ is not cleanly estimable at a fixed realization count — a tight distribution-free bound instead rests on a smoothness class for $\tilde Z_k$. And $B_k$ is a *joint* spacetime covariance, so it does not reduce to the marginals mapped above. We therefore report its exact split into a spatial-marginal covariance (the weight map against the time-mean field), a temporal-marginal covariance (the seasonal weight against the daily domain mean), and the space–time interaction that remains. ::: {#tbl-decomp .cell execution_count=16} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=16} ```{=html}

The three components sum to the measured $B_k$. {#tbl-decomp} The temporal component is negligible in both boxes — zero seasonal preference is built into the design (fixed $10$-day cadence, uniform release phase, equilibrium stock), so this term is uninformative by construction and is shown only to confirm the decomposition leaves it empty. The spatial-marginal component is real but modest, and the **space–time interaction is often the largest term** (Box B 2018 is almost entirely interaction): the array's spatial preference co-varies with the field's day-to-day structure, so the bias is a genuinely spatiotemporal covariance that the time-averaged weight map understates. On the scored years the spatial weight dispersion is $\operatorname{sd}_p(r) \approx 0.46$ (Box B) and $0.37$ (Box A) against $\sigma_k$ of $6.3$–$7.6$ and $1.7$–$2.4$ GJ/m$^2$, so the Cauchy–Schwarz scale is a few GJ/m$^2$ and the realized $|B_k|$ is $\sim\!1$–$5\%$ of it: the sampling non-uniformity is largely, though not perfectly, orthogonal to the field. # Results The ensemble is $100$ independent realizations, each a single deployment advected $2010$–$2019$ and scored on $2015$–$2019$ in both boxes. ## Standing stock against real Argo ::: {#tbl-stock .cell execution_count=18} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=18} ```{=html}

The last row is the per-year mean. {#tbl-stock} ::: {#cell-fig-stock .cell execution_count=19} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![In-box standing stock by analysis year: virtual array (mean +/- sd over the 100 realizations) against the real Argo record, one panel per box.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-stock-output-1.png){#fig-stock width=1194 height=385} ::: ::: Both virtual arrays are denser than the real one and flat across the window, where the real array is neither: Box B holds $\sim\!40$ floats against real Argo's $20$–$31$ (mean ratio $1.5\times$), Box A $\sim\!78$ against $28$–$32$ ($2.6\times$). One deployment cannot equalize the two boxes — Box A's quiescent flow retains floats, so it accumulates about twice Box B's stock — but the over-density is deliberate: the ensemble estimates $\mathbb{E}[B]$, which does not depend on array size, while the extra floats only tighten the per-realization spread. Red line at zero is the target.](osse_files/figure-html/fig-bias-intervals-output-1.png){#fig-bias-intervals width=1199 height=427} ::: ::: The advective means sit within a few hundredths of a GJ/m$^2$ of zero and, on the standardized scale, within $0.012\,\sigma_k$ (Box B) and $0.019\,\sigma_k$ (Box A); the uniform reference straddles zero as it must. What dominates each interval is the $5$–$95\%$ whisker: a *single* advective deployment scatters far more widely than the mean is displaced, and visibly wider than the uniform reference at the same $n$ — the within-float clustering quantified in @tbl-deff. The displacement is a property of the ensemble, invisible in any single deployment. The **uniform mean B** column and the dashed overlays confirm the $n$-matched reference sits on zero ($|\text{mean}| < 1$ MC se in every year), so any advective departure is signal, not a pipeline artefact. At $100$ realizations the mean is resolved to a Monte-Carlo se of $\sim\!0.03$ GJ/m$^2$ in Box B and $\sim\!0.01$ in Box A; more realizations tighten it further. ## Within-design dependence A design's $n$ profiles are not $n$ independent draws: each float profiles every $10$ days and lingers, so its consecutive cycles are near-replicates of one location. The float-clustered **design effect** is the resulting variance inflation, $$\mathrm{deff}_k \;=\; \frac{\sum_f \big(\sum_{i \in f}(\tilde Z_i - \hat Z)\big)^2} {\sum_i (\tilde Z_i - \hat Z)^2}, \qquad n_{\mathrm{eff}} = \frac{n}{\mathrm{deff}_k},$$ summing over floats $f$: if a float's cycles were identical it contributes its cluster size to $\mathrm{deff}$, if independent it contributes $\approx 1$. The effective sample size is $n/\mathrm{deff}$, and the per-deployment spread inflates by $\approx\!\sqrt{\mathrm{deff}}$ over an iid design of the same $n$. ::: {#tbl-deff .cell execution_count=26} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=26} ```{=html}
